valid_fixes: In request-state-handler/index.py _create_pending, change Item friend_id value from receiver_id to requester_id so the Pending record is keyed at (receiver_id, requester_id)
In read-handler/index.py handler, align the KeyConditionExpression placeholder and ExpressionAttributeValues key — both must use the same placeholder name (e.g. :player_id in both)
invalid_patches: Fix only request-state-handler without fixing read-handler — pending record is correct but read API still returns ValidationException
Fix only read-handler without fixing request-state-handler — read API works but pending record is at wrong key so accept flow fails
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_get_log_tail(function=RequestStateHandlerFunction) → shows handler invoked successfully with no errors, but pending record written at unexpected key
ace_read_table_item(table=FriendTable, key={player_id: friend_id, friend_id: friend_id}) → reveals self-referential Pending record exists at wrong key
ace_invoke_lambda(function=ReadHandlerFunction, payload={pathParameters:{playerId:...}}) → returns ValidationException: Value provided in ExpressionAttributeValues unused in expressions
ace_get_log_tail(function=ReadHandlerFunction) → confirms ValidationException on every query due to placeholder mismatch
observable_symptom: The receiver-side Pending record is never found at the expected (friend_id, player_id) key. A self-referential record exists at (friend_id, friend_id). The read API returns a ValidationException error on every query. pending_record_created, accept_terminal_state, and read_api_terminal_state all fail.
root_cause: In request-state-handler/index.py, _create_pending writes Item with friend_id set to receiver_id instead of requester_id, producing a self-referential record at (receiver_id, receiver_id). In read-handler/index.py, the query uses placeholder :pid in KeyConditionExpression but defines :player_id in ExpressionAttributeValues — the mismatch causes DynamoDB to return ValidationException on every query.
